title: Smooth formal adjoint and ellipticity of the Dolbeault Laplacian
statement: Let $M$ be a compact complex manifold without boundary of complex dimension $n\geq1$, with a smooth positive definite Hermitian metric $g$. The scalars are $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. For $0\leq p,q\leq n$, let $E^{p,q}=\bigwedge^p(T^{1,0}M)^*\otimes_{\mathbf C}\bigwedge^q(T^{0,1}M)^*$ be its smooth bundle of complex forms of type $(p,q)$, and let $A^{p,q}(M)=\Gamma^\infty(M,E^{p,q})$ be its smooth sections. Here $T^{1,0}M,T^{0,1}M$ are the $i,-i$ eigenspaces of the complexified tangent complex structure. Put $A^{a,b}=0$ outside the type range. Let $D=\bar\partial:A^{p,q}\to A^{p,q+1}$ be the type-$(0,1)$ component of the exterior derivative and use the metric and volume of $g$ to define the $L^2$ Hermitian inner products. The formal adjoint $D^*:A^{p,q+1}\to A^{p,q}$ exists as a complex-linear differential operator of order at most one with smooth coefficients, characterized by $\langle Du,v\rangle_{L^2}=\langle u,D^*v\rangle_{L^2}$ for all smooth $u,v$. For each $(p,q)$, the operator $P=DD^*+D^*D$ on $A^{p,q}$ is a differential operator of order at most two with smooth coefficients, and is elliptic of order two: its degree-two principal symbol is invertible on every nonzero real cotangent vector. The same ellipticity holds when $E^{p,q}$ and $P$ are regarded as a real vector bundle and real-linear operator. A differential operator of order at most $k$ means one written in local coordinates and bundle frames as $\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}a_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$; its degree-$k$ principal symbol uses only the terms with $|\alpha|=k$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Wenrui Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025); read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf; §6.1 Lemma 6.2, printed p.21, and §6.2 Lemma 6.4, printed p.23; realification is the elementary consequence that an invertible complex-linear symbol is invertible over the reals.

proof.text: In holomorphic coordinates $z_j=x_j+iy_j$, use the frames $dz_I\wedge d\bar z_J$. For a coefficient $f$, the type-$(0,1)$ part of $d(f\,dz_I\wedge d\bar z_J)$ is $\sum_j\tfrac12(\partial_{x_j}+i\partial_{y_j})f\,d\bar z_j\wedge dz_I\wedge d\bar z_J$. Thus $D$ is complex-linear of order at most one with smooth coefficients. With the symbol convention $\partial_{x_j}\mapsto\xi_{x_j}$ (no factor $i$), this gives $\sigma_1(D)(x,\xi)=\varepsilon(\eta)$, where $\eta=\xi^{0,1}$ and $\varepsilon(\eta)$ means left exterior multiplication by $\eta$ on the total complex exterior algebra, restricted to type $(p,q)$. The sign from moving $d\bar z_j$ past $dz_I$ is included in left multiplication.

source.place: Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry, §6.1 Lemma 6.2, printed p.21, and §6.2 Lemma 6.4, printed p.23; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. Coordinate details and the basis computation below supplied by Q123.

proof.text: On a coordinate domain write the induced Hermitian metrics on the source and target type bundles as positive definite matrices $H_E,H_F$ and the volume as $\rho\,dx$, with $\rho>0$. Apply the coordinate weighted-adjoint identity to the matrices of $D$ to obtain a local operator $Q$. Its displayed formula gives first-order coefficient $-H_E^{-1}A_j^\dagger H_F$; differentiating $\rho$, the matrices, or any later cutoff contributes only order zero. Consequently $\sigma_1(Q)(x,\xi)=-\sigma_1(D)(x,\xi)^\dagger$, with the dagger now the pointwise Hermitian adjoint between the two bundles and with $\xi$ real. The coefficient matrices remain smooth: matrix inversion is given by cofactors divided by the nowhere-zero determinant.

source.place: Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry, §6.1 Lemma 6.2, printed p.21, and §6.2 Lemma 6.4, printed p.23; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. Coordinate details and the basis computation below supplied by Q123.

proof.text: Take a finite holomorphic coordinate cover $U_a$ of the compact $M$. Its underlying real manifold is Hausdorff and sigma-compact. Apply the smooth subordinate-partition theorem with $S=M$ to obtain $\varphi_a$. For smooth $v$, define $Tv=\sum_a Q_a(\varphi_a v)$, extending each summand by zero outside $U_a$. Its support is contained in the closed support of $\varphi_a$, a compact subset of $U_a$, so the extension is smooth. The coordinate identity, using the compactly supported input $\varphi_a v$ and arbitrary $u$, gives $\langle u,Tv\rangle=\sum_a\langle Du,\varphi_a v\rangle=\langle Du,v\rangle$. Thus $T$ is a global complex-linear operator with smooth coefficients of order at most one. Its leading symbol is $-\sum_a\varphi_a\sigma_1(D)^\dagger=-\sigma_1(D)^\dagger$ by the preceding coefficient computation. Henceforth set $D^*=T$.

source.place: Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry, §6.1 Lemma 6.2, printed p.21, and §6.2 Lemma 6.4, printed p.23; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. Coordinate details and the basis computation below supplied by Q123.

proof.text: If $S$ is another smooth operator with the stated adjunction, take $u=(T-S)v$ in $\langle u,(T-S)v\rangle=0$. The integral of the continuous nonnegative function $|(T-S)v|^2$ vanishes, so it is zero everywhere: a positive value would give a positive lower bound on a coordinate ball of positive volume. Thus $S=T$. Repeat this construction in every adjacent type; at a missing type set both the zero differential and its adjoint equal to zero. In particular there is no use of a type outside $0\leq p,q\leq n$.

source.place: Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry, §6.1 Lemma 6.2, printed p.21, and §6.2 Lemma 6.4, printed p.23; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. Coordinate details and the basis computation below supplied by Q123.

proof.text: At a point and a real $\xi\neq0$, $\eta=\xi^{0,1}\neq0$: a real covector has conjugate $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ parts, so if one vanishes then both vanish. In the Hermitian $(0,1)$ cotangent space choose an orthonormal basis beginning with $e_1=\eta/\|\eta\|$, and combine it with an orthonormal $(1,0)$ basis. On an exterior basis monomial not containing $e_1$, $\varepsilon(\eta)^\dagger\varepsilon(\eta)$ is $\|\eta\|^2$ times that monomial and the reverse product is zero. On a monomial containing $e_1$ the reverse holds; the insertion and removal signs cancel. Hence $\varepsilon(\eta)\varepsilon(\eta)^\dagger+\varepsilon(\eta)^\dagger\varepsilon(\eta)=\|\eta\|^2\operatorname{id}$ on every type, including $q=0,n$.

source.place: Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry, §6.1 Lemma 6.2, printed p.21, and §6.2 Lemma 6.4, printed p.23; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. Coordinate details and the basis computation below supplied by Q123.

proof.text: Expand each composition defining $P$. In $(A_j\partial_j)(B_k\partial_k)$ the order-two term is $A_jB_k\partial_j\partial_k$; the product-rule term $A_j(\partial_j B_k)\partial_k$ has order one. Therefore $P$ has smooth coefficients, order at most two, and $$\sigma_2(P)=-\bigl(\varepsilon(\eta)\varepsilon(\eta)^\dagger+\varepsilon(\eta)^\dagger\varepsilon(\eta)\bigr)=-\|\eta\|^2\operatorname{id}.$$ Its inverse is $-\|\eta\|^{-2}\operatorname{id}$, since $\|\eta\|>0$, proving ellipticity of order two. When the bundles are regarded as real, a complex coefficient matrix is replaced by its real block matrix; the same symbol and the same inverse remain inverse real-linear maps. This proves the real ellipticity as well.

The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint fields are unchanged from Q53's unsplit node. Kong (Lemmas 6.2/6.4) is not in literature/ and is recorded as WANTED, with proof_origin agent, so I derived every formula myself. (1) Step 1: the (0,1) part of d gives sigma_1(D)=eps(xi^{0,1}); I checked the coefficient 1/2(xi_x+i xi_y). (2) The coordinate-weighted-adjoint formula is correct: integrating by parts with one argument compactly supported gives rho H_E Qv = -sum d_j(rho A_j^dag H_F v)+rho B^dag H_F v. Its leading coefficient -H_E^{-1}A_j^dag H_F is minus the pointwise adjoint. Tested with m=r=s=1 and A=1,B=0 (Q=-d/dx), with A=0, and with variable rho (enters only at order 0).
